dedupe_keys.name: urbanaccess transit and pedestrian network builder for accessibility analysis

description: UrbanAccess is an open-source Python tool that builds multimodal graph networks from GTFS transit feeds and OpenStreetMap pedestrian networks for accessibility analysis at scales from single addresses to whole metropolitan regions, using the network analysis library Pandana. It provides a unified framework for acquiring, validating and processing network data, computing an integrated pedestrian and transit network weighted by schedule-based and time-dependent impedance, and running network analysis with standard node, edge and impedance representations. The README shows integrated AC Transit and BART travel times in Oakland, California. Coverage is generic: any city with GTFS and OpenStreetMap data. Access: free under the AGPL licence from GitHub and PyPI (version 0.2.2); the README lists its status as active. Caveats: accessibility depends on the quality and period of the GTFS feeds used, and it prepares networks, not simulating traffic. It supports public transport accessibility and equity studies, service disruption scenarios by removing routes or stops, and network flow inputs, and complements the Mobility Database and OSMnx catalogued here.
name: UrbanAccess, transit and pedestrian network builder for accessibility analysis
outputs: integrated transit and pedestrian network graph
